newsitem.title: INDIA: Bomb blast injures six in India's Punjab state.
newsitem.headline: Bomb blast injures six in India's Punjab state.

text.p: A powerful bomb blast near a train station injured at least six people in India's northern state of Punjab on Friday, the United News of India (UNI) said.
The news agency quoted witnesses at the site of the blast in the city of Jalandhar as saying they saw at least six people lying on the ground after the explosion.
Police in Jalandhar gave no further details but said they were investigating the bomb explosion, UNI said.
Sikh militants fighting for an independent homeland in the agriculture-rich region have frequently targeted trains there, usually inflicting serious casualties.
A pro-Sikh government took power in Punjab following a rare peaceful election for the state legislature in February, apparently ending years of separatist violence.

More than 20,000 people have died in Punjab since discontent with New Delhi turned into an armed insurrection after the government sent in troops to flush out militants holed up inside the Golden Temple in Amritsar, the Sikhs' holiest shrine, in June 1984.
